judge_output.rationale: No listed work measures 3.05/3.29/3.4/4.27/4.67 um band equivalent widths with SPHEREx across the union of WISE waste-heat candidate lists. However, Hephaistos IV (2026arXiv260709460Z) already used JWST/MIRI spectroscopy on two Hephaistos candidates and attributed their excesses to background galaxies with Hot DOG and dusty-starburst spectra. That is a spectral test of whether the excess is natural, but on only two sources, with a different instrument and wavelength range. Other follow-ups (Ren 2026, Korn 2026, Ren 2024, Blain 2024) addressed contamination through astrometry, radio data, imaging or stellar parameters rather than solid-state or molecular band strengths, so the card's population-wide SPHEREx band census remains largely untested.

closest_prior.relation: JWST/MIRI imaging and spectroscopy of Hephaistos candidates D and E found background Hot DOG and dusty-starburst spectra; it is a spectral natural-origin test on 2 sources in the mid-IR, not SPHEREx 2-5 um band EWs for the full candidate union.

Archival astrometric, imaging and radio diagnostics of nine Hephaistos candidates for background contamination; no spectral band measurements, and candidates D and I remain without obvious contamination.
Photometric and some spectroscopic characterisation of ten candidates (youth indicators, H-alpha, stellar parameters), leaving the excess unexplained; it does not test dust-band features.
Source of the WISE excess candidate list, which the card would test spectroscopically; the excess was assessed only through broadband SED fits.

judge_output.what_would_make_it_open: No listed work delivers SPHEREx forced-photometry spectra with injection-calibrated equivalent widths or upper limits on the H2O, PAH, aliphatic, CO2 and CO bands for the full union of published WISE waste-heat candidate lists (Hephaistos, the G-hat red galaxies and others), together with a sorting into feature-bearing and featureless sources.
